title: Applied ML Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook documents Redwood Inference's recommended end-to-end processes for the eval harness, prompt set and benchmark curation, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profile management, and regression triage. It is intended for Applied ML engineers, model owners, SREs who operate inference infrastructure, and product owners who monitor behavioral regressions.

Scope: Covers onboarding new models into the eval harness, defining benchmark and prompt set standards, producing quantization profiles compatible with the serving runtime, setting quality guardrails and alerts, and a standard regression triage workflow with owner assignments and SLAs.

Quick links
- Eval harness standards: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Quantization profiles guidance: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026
- Regression triage runbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/applied-ml-regression-triage-playbook-2026.json

Principles
- Treat evaluations as code: tests and prompt sets live in version control with CI gating.
- Guardrails first: automated checks before any rollout; human-reviewed checks for major behavioral changes.
- Traceability: every regression must be traceable to a commit, model version, prompt set change, or infrastructure change.
- Lowest-cost safe path: prefer lightweight checks (embedding drift, scalar metrics) to decide triage urgency before running full eval sweeps.

Roles & ownership
- Model owner (Applied ML): maintains prompt sets, model config, quantization profiles, and gating thresholds.
- Eval harness owner (Applied ML infra): maintains harness code, CI integrations, test runner, and tooling to run batches.
- Observability / SRE: defines monitor dashboards, traces, and alert routing for production signal degradations.
- Product / PM: defines user-facing quality targets and test sets for critical flows.

Eval harness onboarding checklist (required before a model can be promoted to staging)
1) Register model in model-catalog with metadata: architecture, tokenizer, expected max context, training data summary, and supported quantization points.
2) Produce a baseline eval run: run the eval harness on the canonical prompt set (see 'Prompt sets' below) and record: throughput, median latency (p50/p95), perplexity, and top-line behavioral metrics. Attach the run ID to the model entry.
3) Add unit-level automated tests: tokenization round-trip, deterministic seeds for sampling-sensitive tests, and end-to-end smoke generation for 3 representative prompts.
4) Submit quantization profile (if applicable) and validate accuracy bounds (see 'Quantization profiles' section).
5) CI gating: add the model to the CI matrix for nightly evals and to the pull request checks for any code or prompt changes that reference the model.

Prompt sets and benchmarks
- Prompt taxonomy: split prompts into categories: functional (API correctness), safety (attack simulations), instruction-following, domain-specific (customer verticals), and edge-cases (long context, ambiguous queries).
- Minimum prompt set for onboarding: 500 prompts distributed across categories, with labels for expected output type and automated scoring function where possible.
- Benchmark metrics: exact match (for closed tasks), BLEU/ROUGE (where applicable), embedding-similarity for semantic tasks (cosine similarity using reference embedding), and custom downstream task metrics (e.g., reranking NDCG).
- Prompt set governance: prompts are stored in a canonical repo with metadata: source, author, tags, expected-output, and scoring script. Changes to prompt sets require a PR with at least one reviewer and a CI run that reproduces baseline metrics.

Quality guardrails (automated + human)
- Automated gates (fail fast):
  - Latency: p95 must not regress >20% relative to baseline for same hardware and sequence distribution.
  - Embedding drift: average reference cosine similarity drop >0.05 triggers a medium alert.
  - Output token safety: safety-policy violation rate increase >0.1% triggers immediate hold.
  - Critical metric degradation: if downstream critical metric (e.g., conversion rate proxy) drops >3%, escalate to SEV-1 process.
- Human review gates: any change that increases hallucination indicators or reduces factuality by >5% (per eval harness factuality suite) requires a documented mitigation plan and sign-off by the model owner and the product PM.

Quantization profiles and validation
- Profiles: define quantization points (e.g., fp16, int8 Static, int8 Dynamic, custom 4-bit) with associated transformation steps and expected accuracy delta budgets.
- Baseline acceptance criteria: accuracy delta (task-specific) must be within configured budget (default: <= 1.5% relative for aggregate metrics; for sensitive tasks, <= 0.5%).
- Validation suite: run the full prompt set plus an adversarial focused subset of 200 difficulty prompts. Record metric deltas per category.
- Performance checks: measure throughput, memory (GPU/CPU), and p50/p95 latency. Quantized profile should meet target cost/latency trade-offs defined in the model entry.
- Packaging: quantization artifacts and a short README (commands to reproduce) must be committed to the model repo and referenced from the model catalog entry.

Regression triage workflow
1) Detect: regression can be detected from CI eval failures, production monitors, or customer reports. Severity mapping:
   - SEV-1: showstopper affecting many customers or causing incorrect outputs with safety implications. Response goal: acknowledgement 15min, mitigation or rollback 1 hour.
   - SEV-2: noticeable user-impact or metric degradation (e.g., major drop in NPS proxy). Response goal: acknowledgement 1 hour, mitigation 4 hours.
   - SEV-3: minor regressions or single-feature degradations. Response goal: acknowledgement 24 hours.
2) Triage: initial triage owner (automated: alert routing uses runbook mapping) runs quick checks:
   - Verify instrumentation: are the metrics up-to-date? Is sampling representative?
   - Correlate to changes: check recent model promotions, infra deployment, quantization profile changes, prompt set PRs, and code merges in the last 24–72 hours.
   - Run a narrow eval sweep: 50 high-signal prompts across affected categories to establish repro.
3) Contain: if SEV-1/SEV-2 and repro is high-confidence, take mitigation: rollback model or apply config-based fallback (route to fallback model variant or reduce temperature and sampling).
4) Root cause analysis (RCA): full RCA should include: diff of model weights (if available), quantization diff artifacts, prompt set diffs, infra config diffs, and CI run logs. Attach findings to the incident ticket.
5) Remediation and prevention: create follow-up tasks for code fixes, additional tests, improved monitoring, or model retraining. Add new automatic tests to the eval harness where appropriate.
6) Postmortem: SEV-1 and SEV-2 incidents require a postmortem with timeline, impact, root cause, remediation, and retro actions.

CI integration and automation
- Gate matrix: PR checks must run fast smoke tests (tokenization, 10-sample generation) and schedule longer nightly runs (full prompt set). Failures of critical metrics on PR must block merge.
- Canary rollout: use staged rollout to internal staging and 5% production traffic for 24 hours with active monitoring before full promotion. Canary must run the same eval harness as staging with synthetic load mirroring production.
- Regression detection pipeline: nightly delta detector computes metric deltas per model and posts alerts to the regression triage Slack channel with run links and diffs.

Monitoring & dashboards (minimum set)
- Model health dashboard (per-model): throughput, p50/p95 latency, per-category accuracy, embed drift, safety violation rate, recent PRs and model-version tags.
- Regression detector dashboard: trending metric deltas with rolling 7/30/90 day windows.

Operational runbooks and playbooks (links)
- Quick rollback: steps to pin traffic to previous model variant and clear caches.
- Fallback routing: config examples for routing policy that sends traffic to a smaller but more stable model variant on high-latency or safety violation signals.

Examples & reproducible commands
- Run a targeted eval sweep (example):
  conda activate eval-harness && python run_eval.py --model=my-model:v1 --prompts=prompts/staging/high-signal-50.json --output=results/v1-quick-sweep.json

- Validate quantization profile (example):
  ./quantize.sh --model model.pt --profile profiles/int8-dynamic.yaml --output model-int8.pt
  python run_eval.py --model=model-int8.pt --prompts=prompts/adversarial-200.json --compare-to=baseline/v1.json

Open decisions and constraints
- Decision: default embedding drift threshold set to 0.05 for trio of reference datasets (general, domain-specific, and safety). This value was chosen to balance sensitivity vs. false positives.
- Constraint: nightly full-eval budget is limited to 10x baseline runtime across all models to control cost; aggressive evaluation must be scheduled and approved.

Appendix: example metric table (onboarding baseline)
| Metric | Baseline | Acceptance | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p50 latency (ms) | 120 | <=144 (<=20% increase) | measured on g4dn.xlarge equivalent |
| p95 latency (ms) | 420 | <=504 | |
| Embedding cosine (avg) | 0.87 | >=0.82 | lower indicates drift |
| Safety violation rate | 0.02% | <=0.12% | fail fast threshold |
| Aggregate accuracy (task suite) | 86.1% | >=84.6% | 1.5% allowed delta |
